text:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: streaming decode cluster (us-west-2) - multiple GPU OOMs during high-throughput chat generation. request drops observed, alerting pager @sre-oncall-amy

sre-oncall-amy: on it. grabbing logs now, assigning initial triage. tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml.

olivia-runtime: seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` on decode-worker-3 and decode-worker-7. containers are OOMKilled then restart loop. looks correlated with large user requests (long max_tokens).

jordan-ml: metric: token-rate spike ~x6 for a subset of clients 11:12-11:18. some requests had header `max_tokens: 20000` - suspect runaway generation + header mismatch with token cap enforcement.

emma-custops: we have two customer tickets referencing 11:15 failures, CS triage in progress. notifying impacted tenants.

sre-oncall-amy: immediate mitigation: enable per-route hard token ceiling (1000) at the router to drop / short-circuit dangerous requests. deploying now.

ops-bot: deploy start: route-config-upsert (token-ceil=1000) by sre-oncall-amy — please monitor.

olivia-runtime: applied. router is returning 429 for requests exceeding 1000 tokens. we still see OOMs but freq reduced, some nodes still crash (KV cache growth lingering).

jordan-ml: can we enable fallback to cpu-decode-compat variant for inflight long-horizon requests? that will increase latency but avoid GPU crash.

sre-oncall-amy: initiating canary fallback policy to route new oversized requests to cpu-decode-compat, but let existing sessions drain. patching rollout now.

olivia-runtime: started drain on decode-worker-3 (cordon + SIGTERM). mounting memory profile: flamegraph shows KV cache spike from a single request id `req_8f7b` — looks like prompt loop.

jordan-ml: adding short-term token-based rate limit per client (burst 2000 / minute) to prevent fanout storms. pushing rule.

ops-bot: rate-limit rule applied for clients matching `plg-*` pattern.

emma-custops: informing customers: CS draft ready, will send proactive note: "we mitigated OOM risk, some requests may have been dropped or slowed; we're following up with root cause and ticket links."

olivia-runtime: root cause hypothesis: upstream client-edge was not honoring `max_tokens` override causing runaway generation; our router used to trust client headers for token ceiling in some legacy routes. filing PR to enforce server-side max cap enforcement.

sre-oncall-amy: current status: crash rate down from 8/hr to 0.5/hr after router-enforced ceiling + cpu-fallback; nodes recovering, restarts stable. keeping pager active for 2h.

jordan-ml: follow-ups: 1) force server-side override for token cap in router (hotfix merged) 2) add telemetry alert on per-request token request > configured cap 3) postmortem + customer-impact list.

emma-custops: will compile impacted tenant list and draft CS notes. prepping AM update.

olivia-runtime: logs attached in thread (snip):
```
[11:15:32] decode-worker-3 ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: allocation failed for kv_cache size=14GB, request_id=req_8f7b
[11:15:35] docker: container OOMKilled, exit_code=137
[11:16:01] router WARN: request exceeded token_ceiling (client-max 20000, server-cap 1000) - shortcircuit -> 429
```

sre-oncall-amy: tagging for postmortem: eng-runtime (olivia), eng-ml (jordan), custops (emma), infra-sre. I'll start the incident timeline doc.

ops-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV2 — customer impact limited to a small set of tenants; mitigation in place.

olivia-runtime: note: need to garbage-collect stale KV entries faster and add soft-limits for cache growth per session to avoid slow memory bleed during heavy tail sessions. filing backlog ticket.

jordan-ml: will add a unit-test / e2e for header-cap mismatch cases and a regression alert in the evals suite.

emma-custops: sending initial CS note in 10m. will include timeline and mitigation steps.

sre-oncall-amy: thanks team. oncall will monitor for 2 hours and then hand back to rotations. postmortem P0 for follow-up tasks.

incident-bot: resolved: mitigation verified. please update incident log and attach customer comms when ready. :white_check_mark:
